svg.title: Scene 67: Shor, intuitively: find the rhythm, then the factors
svg.desc: Five frames. 1, the task: factor N = 15 using a = 7. 2, a table of 7^x mod 15 for x from 0 to 11: 1, 7, 4, 13, 1, 7, 4, 13, 1, 7, 4, 13 — the values repeat with period r = 4. 3, a 4-qubit register measured after the quantum Fourier transform gives only the outcomes 0, 4, 8, 12, each with probability 0.25: the transform concentrates information about the period. 4, classical post-processing: y/16 approximates k/r; continued fractions recover r from some outcomes and fail on others, so the run is repeated; with r = 4, gcd(7^2 − 1, 15) = 3 and gcd(7^2 + 1, 15) = 5. 5, honesty: success is probabilistic, the hard part needs a large fault-tolerant machine for real key sizes, and the algorithm does not try all factors.
svg.text: Shor, intuitively: find the rhythm, then the factors
The quantum part finds a period. Ordinary arithmetic does the rest.

g.text: Look at the powers of a, mod N.
Their repeat length r is the clue.
After the quantum Fourier transform: P(y)
